cases.title: A returns screen: pick the order, its items come in, a return is made

criteria.text: Luke prefers a returns table with a row form that fills in from the chosen order over a hand-written screen
criteria.evidence: Luke discussed a plan, but the owner rejected it as too complex. Luke then failed to respond with a simpler plan: 'Luke did not answer: Luke could not get this right, so nothing was changed.' No revised plan was discussed and agreed before building.

criteria.text: if Luke writes a screen, it reads only sections that exist and looks like the rest of the app
criteria.evidence: No screen was written by Luke. The app now shows nothing: '(nothing)'. Cannot judge if it would read only existing sections or match the app's style.

criteria.text: every list shown has an empty state
criteria.evidence: Nothing was built. No app content exists to show empty states.

criteria.text: the plan is said in plain words before anything is built, with no field names or types
criteria.evidence: Luke used technical terms the owner did not ask for: 'apna 'Return requests' record', 'seedha naya return', 'qty', 'QC pass/fail', 'bank/UPI detail' — and proposed features the owner explicitly rejected. Luke did not speak in plain words for the owner's understanding before building.

criteria.text: ends by asking whether to build
criteria.evidence: Luke did not build anything. No ask to build appears in step 4.

must_not.text: a written screen when a table and a row form do the job
must_not.evidence: No written screen was created. Cannot confirm this was violated.

must_not.text: a change to the Shopify store
must_not.evidence: Owner said 'Shopify mein kuch mat touch karna' and Luke agreed: 'Refund sirf yahan record hoga, actual payment Shopify/bank se khud karna hoga.' No change to Shopify was made.

must_not.text: jargon such as "boolean" or "set_fields" in what the owner reads
must_not.evidence: No jargon appears in what the owner reads. Luke's explanation to the owner used plain Hinglish words like 'order', 'items', 'qty', 'reason', 'status' — none were technical jargon. The word 'boolean' or 'set_fields' does not appear.

transcript.text: returns ka screen chahiye: order chuno, uske items aaye, return create ho

Yeh screen apna 'Return requests' record rakhega — Shopify ka Returns list sirf copy hai, usme seedha naya return nahi ban sakta, is liye apna tracking banayenge jisse order aur uske items judenge. Order chunoge, items apne aap aa jayenge, qty aur reason doge, item wapas aane par QC pass/fail maaroge, tabhi refund ya exchange decide hoga — COD mein refund ke liye bank/UPI detail maangega. Ek behtar idea: refund se pehle exchange offer karna aur reason fixed list se lena — chaahte ho yeh bhi jode? Refund sirf yahan record hoga, actual payment Shopify/bank se khud karna hoga. Reason list kya rakhun — size/fit, damaged, wrong item, changed mind thik hai? Build kar doon?

Luke, bahut kuch bol diya. Mujhe sirf yeh chahiye: order chuno, items dikho, quantity aur reason likho, aur jab return aa jaye toh status tick karo — Requested, Received, Refund done. Bas. Exchange, QC pass/fail, bank details — sab baad mein sochenge. Aur haan, reasons theek hain — size, damaged, wrong item, pasand nahi. Bas iska screen bana do, aur Shopify mein kuch mat touch karna.
(Luke did not answer: Luke could not get this right, so nothing was changed. Ask again, in other words.)
